cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Approve the Cover Story
cards.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Can you approve 'delivery delay' in the newsletter? I don't want our new volunteer blamed for the melted cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She delivered it on time. We left it by the radiator.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then 'storage problem'. Will you approve that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if we mention the refund.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. 'Storage problem; full refund arranged.' Can I put your name under it?

mechanism: A approves revisions to a protective public explanation while directing B to endorse the final text.
confusable: Unlike ordinary copyediting, A aims to protect a person and secure another name behind the explanation.
comparison: Volunteer cake blame and refund differ from hall-access protection and key admission.
seedUse: Use delivery versus storage correction and refund condition; let A retain editorial rank while obtaining B's signature.
